title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after the deterministic validator and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as the paired difference in success rates per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations) is not supported given the observed baseline error prevalence. We correct contingency-cell labeling, clarify provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair), add extensive artifact-grounded methodological and reproducibility details, and explicitly document reviewer requests that cannot be satisfied verbatim from the supplied manuscript bundle while pointing auditors to the exact archived artifacts (paths and SHA-256 digests) needed to compute those values.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) promise to translate operator intent into device-specific network configuration, enabling faster change cycles and lower operational cost. However, incorrect device commands can cause outages; therefore, many proposals insert deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in the generate→verify→repair (GVR) architecture. Despite widespread recommendation, rigorous preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit of deterministic validators under an explicit adapter contract (bounded repair budget, single hosted model) is rare and often lacks full cryptographic artifact traceability. Our preregistered research question (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) asked: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types remain after automated repairs? We emphasize paired estimand choice (within-task comparison) to control for task difficulty heterogeneity. Key high-level contribution: a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces, transparent provider-call accounting, and a forensic archive for auditors.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime checkers (e.g., header-space analysis and VeriFlow) provide a long precedent for pre-deployment checks; recent work applies LLMs to intent→configuration translation and NetOps automation but often omits preregistration or complete artifact hashing. Representative prior work motivating our study includes static and incremental network verification methods (Kazemian et al., header-space; Khurshid et al., VeriFlow) and empirical LLM-for-NetOps evaluations (NetConfEval and intent-driven configuration generators). Unlike typical leaderboard-style evaluations, our study is confirmatory and paired: we hold the initial LLM candidate fixed and compare the final guarded output after deterministic validation and the adapter-enforced single repair attempt. We also provide full cryptographic artifact traceability to support forensic audits.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. The preregistration cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 froze a paired binary design (N=200 tasks) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each task the validator marks baseline and guarded outputs as actionable-error ∈ {0,1}; we operationalize success = 1 − actionable_error and report the paired difference guarded_success_rate − baseline_success_rate. This algebraic mapping implies: a reduction in actionable-error rate equals an increase in success rate (guarded − baseline). The preregistration also specified confirmatory test (exact McNemar two-sided) and a paired bootstrap CI procedure (resamples=10000, seed=1729). The preregistration and its SHA-256 are archived (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4).

Adapter contract, model, and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial candidate per task) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider_call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) and shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, matching model_calls_used = 201 in execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02).

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. The study used a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor intent bank (preregistered sampling-plan stratification across three vendor families: Cisco-like 66, Juniper-like 67, RFC-neutral 67) and task templates executed by a deterministic task generator. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parsed generated artifacts into canonical ASTs, enforced intent-constraint checks, dependency/workflow policies, and simulator-based semantic checks; each episode records validation_before and validation_after traces and a binary score ∈ {0,1}. Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are the authoritative scoring records; a representative set of those per-episode JSONs and their SHA-256 digests are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement.

Execution accounting, retries, and missingness. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures and specified conservative sensitivity analyses treating technical failures as actionable errors. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200 (see execution manifest and analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c).

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory analysis used the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (input SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) to compute the 2×2 contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10000). We preserved the preregistered multiplicity policy (single primary hypothesis; secondary/exploratory tests labeled as exploratory). All analysis artifacts and CSVs are archived with SHA-256 digests cited below.
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded): Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) are: n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0, guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both 0). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d).

Estimand and hypothesis reconciliation (required revision resolved). The preregistered primary_estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered hypothesis language invoked a 50% relative reduction in actionable misconfiguration rate; by algebra the reduction in actionable-error rate equals guarded_success_rate − baseline_success_rate. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction would correspond to an absolute reduction of 0.0025 (0.25 percentage points), far smaller than the original power calculation target (absolute 0.15) used in the preregistration. Thus the preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially higher baseline error prevalence than was observed; this mismatch explains why the preregistered confirmatory threshold (designed for larger absolute effects) is not met even though the observed absolute change is an improvement. We explicitly correct previous ambiguous language and report the exact algebraic mapping and observed counts above; all artifacts are archived and hashed.

Representative artifact examples and forensic pointers. Representative per-episode scoring JSONs and shared-initial/raw response files are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ with SHA-256 digests; three representative tasks (task-000001..000006) and their file digests are included in the manuscript evidence bundle. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is present in the archived raw results; auditors can locate the explicit episode identifier by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) or by inspecting execution/scoring/ JSONs (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because the explicit episode id string is not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript bundle, we do not invent it in text but provide the direct artifact digests and paths for auditors.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator v5, and adapter-enforced single repair), the guarded pipeline produced a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced very few actionable errors (1/200). Deterministic validators remain operationally valuable for canonicalization, auditability, and occasional repair invocations in higher-error regimes; realized ROI will depend on baseline generator error prevalence, validator coverage, repair budget, human-in-the-loop costs, and risk tolerance.

Power, estimand alignment, and design lessons. The preregistered power calculation targeted a large absolute effect (detect absolute reduction 0.15) assuming a much higher baseline actionable-error rate. The observed baseline error rate (=0.005) implies the original design lacked power to declare confirmatory support of a 50% relative reduction despite observing an actual guarded improvement. Future confirmatory designs seeking to validate small relative improvements should either increase N, enrich for tasks with higher baseline error prevalence, or relax paired design constraints to attain sufficient discordant-pair mass.

Resolved reviewer issues and remaining computable items. We resolved the manuscript ambiguity about estimand directionality and corrected contingency-cell notation (the archived CSV header is 'guarded,baseline,count'; we define n_11=guarded=1 & baseline=1, etc.; CSV SHA-256 = 658051ba...). The reviewer requests for (1) per-vendor stratified observed counts and (2) verbatim discordant episode id are computable from archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a and execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Because neither value appears verbatim in the supplied manuscript bundle text, we do not fabricate them; auditors can derive them from the cited artifacts. We explicitly record these reviewer requests as unresolved in-manuscript but fully answerable from the archive (artifact paths and SHA-256 digests provided in the Disclosure Statement and in the evidence bundle). This choice preserves forensic traceability and avoids inventing numbers not present verbatim in the provided manuscript evidence bundle.

Failure-mode and contamination analysis. Contamination checks and validator-flag clustering produced no systematic contamination signals (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...), and missingness_summary.csv records zero model-call failures. The deterministic_reconciliation.json shows provider_call_audit stage_counts consistent with a single repair invocation across the run. Because post-repair guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2) comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed as a confirmatory test; any error-type discussion is therefore exploratory and limited by absence of guarded failures.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline with bounded repair budget. On our synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under the original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far lower than assumed during power planning. We provide full cryptographic hashes and artifact pointers for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can reproduce contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived execution manifest and raw results. Future work should expand model coverage, validator diversity, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair yields material operational risk reduction.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), but we do not invent or assert specific per-vendor numbers or an episode id in the manuscript where those values are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
